passages.text: Then the LORD said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it with an ordinary stylus: Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a command.
He said, "Take a large scroll."
He told me to use an ordinary stylus.
He said, "Write these words: Maher-shalal-hash-baz."
Maher-shalal-hash-baz means 'quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil.'
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י קַח־ לְךָ֖ גִּלָּי֣וֹן גָּד֑וֹל וּכְתֹ֤ב עָלָיו֙ בְּחֶ֣רֶט אֱנ֔וֹשׁ לְמַהֵ֥ר שָׁלָ֖ל חָ֥שׁ בַּֽז׃

passages.text: And I will appoint for Myself trustworthy witnesses—Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Isaiah.
God said He would appoint witnesses for Himself.
God chose Uriah.
Uriah was a priest.
God also chose Zechariah.
Zechariah was the son of Jeberekiah.
God called both men trustworthy witnesses.
passages.original: וְאָעִ֣ידָה לִּ֔י עֵדִ֖ים נֶאֱמָנִ֑ים אֵ֚ת אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֶת־ זְכַרְיָ֖הוּ בֶּ֥ן יְבֶרֶכְיָֽהוּ׃

passages.text: And I had relations with the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. The LORD said to me, “Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
passages.sermon:
I am Isaiah the prophet.
I went to the prophetess.
She became pregnant.
She gave birth to a son.
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD told me to name the boy Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
passages.original: וָאֶקְרַב֙ אֶל־ הַנְּבִיאָ֔ה וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י קְרָ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ מַהֵ֥ר שָׁלָ֖ל חָ֥שׁ בַּֽז׃

passages.text: For before the boy knows how to cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to Isaiah the prophet.
Isaiah had a son named Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
The Lord gave a message about this boy.
The boy is very young.
He does not yet know how to say ‘Father’ or ‘Mother.’
Before the boy learns to say these words, something will happen.
The king of Assyria will come.
He will take away the wealth of Damascus.
He will also take the plunder of Samaria.
This will happen soon, before the boy grows up.
passages.original: כִּ֗י בְּטֶ֙רֶם֙ יֵדַ֣ע הַנַּ֔עַר קְרֹ֖א אָבִ֣י וְאִמִּ֑י יִשָּׂ֣א׀ אֶת־ חֵ֣יל דַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק וְאֵת֙ שְׁלַ֣ל שֹׁמְר֔וֹן לִפְנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃ס

passages.text: And the LORD spoke to me further: “Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah, the Lord will surely bring against them the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates — the king of Assyria and all his pomp. It will overflow its channels and overrun its banks.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me again.
He said these words to me.
This people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah.
They have chosen not to trust in what is peaceful and quiet.
They have rejoiced in Rezin.
They have rejoiced in the son of Remaliah.
Because of this, the Lord will act against them.
The Lord will bring the mighty and great waters of the river against them.
These waters mean the king of Assyria and all his glory.
The king of Assyria will come with all his power.
He will overflow every channel.
He will run over every bank.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר׃ יַ֗עַן כִּ֤י מָאַס֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֵ֚ת מֵ֣י הַשִּׁלֹ֔חַ הַהֹלְכִ֖ים לְאַ֑ט וּמְשׂ֥וֹשׂ אֶת־ רְצִ֖ין וּבֶן־ רְמַלְיָֽהוּ׃ וְלָכֵ֡ן הִנֵּ֣ה אֲדֹנָי֩ מַעֲלֶ֨ה עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־ מֵ֣י הַנָּהָ֗ר הָעֲצוּמִים֙ וְהָ֣רַבִּ֔ים אֶת־ מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר וְאֶת־ כָּל־ כְּבוֹד֑וֹ וְעָלָה֙ עַל־ כָּל־ אֲפִיקָ֔יו וְהָלַ֖ךְ עַל־ כָּל־ גְּדוֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: It will pour into Judah, swirling and sweeping over it, reaching up to the neck; its spreading streams will cover your entire land, O Immanuel!
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria will invade Judah.
He will come like a flood.
He will sweep through the land.
The flood will rise high.
It will reach up to the neck.
His power will spread wide.
His armies will cover your whole land.
O Immanuel, your land will be filled.
passages.original: וְחָלַ֤ף בִּֽיהוּדָה֙ שָׁטַ֣ף וְעָבַ֔ר עַד־ צַוָּ֖אר יַגִּ֑יעַ וְהָיָה֙ מֻטּ֣וֹת כְּנָפָ֔יו מְלֹ֥א רֹֽחַב־ אַרְצְךָ֖ עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Huddle together, O peoples, and be shattered; pay attention, all you distant lands; prepare for battle, and be shattered; prepare for battle, and be shattered!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to all nations.
He warns every people, near and far.
Gather together, all you nations.
You will be broken.
Listen, all distant lands.
Prepare yourselves for war.
You will be broken.
Prepare again for battle.
You will be broken.
passages.original: רֹ֤עוּ עַמִּים֙ וָחֹ֔תּוּ וְהַֽאֲזִ֔ינוּ כֹּ֖ל מֶרְחַקֵּי־ אָ֑רֶץ הִתְאַזְּר֣וּ וָחֹ֔תּוּ הִֽתְאַזְּר֖וּ וָחֹֽתּוּ׃

passages.text: Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; state a proposal, but it will not happen. For God is with us.”
passages.sermon:
People may make plans.
People may speak words and make proposals.
Their plans will fail.
Their proposals will not succeed.
God is with us.
passages.original: עֻ֥צוּ עֵצָ֖ה וְתֻפָ֑ר דַּבְּר֤וּ דָבָר֙ וְלֹ֣א יָק֔וּם כִּ֥י עִמָּ֖נוּ אֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD has spoken to me with a strong hand, instructing me not to walk in the way of this people: “Do not call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He spoke with a strong hand.
He gave me a command.
He told me not to live like these people.
He said, “Do not call everything a conspiracy.
These people call many things a conspiracy.
Do not fear what they fear.
Do not be afraid like they are.
Do not live in dread.”
passages.original: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י כְּחֶזְקַ֣ת הַיָּ֑ד וְיִסְּרֵ֕נִי מִלֶּ֛כֶת בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ הָֽעָם־ הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ לֹא־ תֹאמְר֣וּן קֶ֔שֶׁר לְכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־ יֹאמַ֛ר הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה קָ֑שֶׁר וְאֶת־ מוֹרָא֥וֹ לֹֽא־ תִֽירְא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א תַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts is the One you shall regard as holy. Only He should be feared; only He should be dreaded.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
God commands great armies.
You must treat God as holy.
You must fear only God.
You must dread only God.
passages.original: אֶת־ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֹת֣וֹ תַקְדִּ֑ישׁוּ וְה֥וּא מוֹרַאֲכֶ֖ם וְה֥וּא מַֽעֲרִֽצְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And He will be a sanctuary— but to both houses of Israel a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, to the dwellers of Jerusalem a trap and a snare.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is holy.
He will be a sanctuary.
He will be a stone that makes both houses of Israel stumble.
He will be a rock that causes them to fall.
He will be a trap for the people who live in Jerusalem.
He will be a snare for them.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֖ה לְמִקְדָּ֑שׁ וּלְאֶ֣בֶן נֶ֠גֶף וּלְצ֨וּר מִכְשׁ֜וֹל לִשְׁנֵ֨י בָתֵּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְפַ֣ח וּלְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ לְיוֹשֵׁ֖ב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Many will stumble over these; they will fall and be broken; they will be ensnared and captured.”
passages.sermon:
Many people will stumble over these things.
They will fall.
They will be broken.
They will be trapped.
They will be captured.
passages.original: וְכָ֥שְׁלוּ בָ֖ם רַבִּ֑ים וְנָפְל֣וּ וְנִשְׁבָּ֔רוּ וְנוֹקְשׁ֖וּ וְנִלְכָּֽדוּ׃ס

passages.text: Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His prophet Isaiah.
God commands Isaiah to act.
God says, “Bind up the testimony.”
God says, “Seal the law.”
God says, “Keep these things among my disciples.”
Isaiah must protect God’s message.
Isaiah must keep God’s teaching safe with those who learn from him.

passages.text: I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. I will put my trust in Him.
passages.sermon: The LORD hides His face from the house of Jacob.\r\nI will wait for the LORD.\r\nI will put my trust in Him.
passages.original: וְחִכִּ֙יתִי֙ לַיהוָ֔ה הַמַּסְתִּ֥יר פָּנָ֖יו מִבֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְקִוֵּ֖יתִֽי־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me as signs and symbols in Israel from the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah is speaking.
Isaiah stands before the people.
Isaiah says, “Here I am.”
Isaiah has children.
The LORD gave these children to Isaiah.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is called the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD lives on Mount Zion.
Isaiah and his children are signs in Israel.
Isaiah and his children are symbols in Israel.
The LORD gave Isaiah and his children for this purpose.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י וְהַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־ לִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְאֹת֥וֹת וּלְמוֹפְתִ֖ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מֵעִם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הַשֹּׁכֵ֖ן בְּהַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ס

passages.text: When men tell you to consult the spirits of the dead and the spiritists who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
passages.sermon:
Some people may tell you to seek advice from mediums.
Some people may tell you to seek advice from spiritists.
Mediums claim to speak with the dead.
Spiritists whisper and mutter.
God’s people should seek guidance from their God.
People should not ask the dead for help for the living.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם דִּרְשׁ֤וּ אֶל־ הָאֹבוֹת֙ וְאֶל־ הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים הַֽמְצַפְצְפִ֖ים וְהַמַּהְגִּ֑ים הֲלוֹא־ עַם֙ אֶל־ אֱלֹהָ֣יו יִדְרֹ֔שׁ בְּעַ֥ד הַחַיִּ֖ים אֶל־ הַמֵּתִֽים׃

passages.text: To the law and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, they have no light of dawn.
passages.sermon:
God gave His law and His testimony to Israel.
God wants people to listen to His law and His testimony.
If someone does not speak according to God's word, they do not have light.
They do not have the light of dawn.
They remain in darkness.
passages.original: לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה אִם־ לֹ֤א יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽין־ ל֖וֹ שָֽׁחַר׃

passages.text: They will roam the land, dejected and hungry. When they are famished, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.
passages.sermon:
The people will walk through the land.
They will feel troubled.
They will be hungry.
When they are hungry, they will become angry.
They will curse their king.
They will curse their God.
They will look upward.
passages.original: וְעָ֥בַר בָּ֖הּ נִקְשֶׁ֣ה וְרָעֵ֑ב וְהָיָ֨ה כִֽי־ יִרְעַ֜ב וְהִתְקַצַּ֗ף וְקִלֵּ֧ל בְּמַלְכּ֛וֹ וּבֵאלֹהָ֖יו וּפָנָ֥ה לְמָֽעְלָה׃

passages.text: Then they will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish. And they will be driven into utter darkness.
passages.sermon:
The people will look at the earth.
They will see distress.
They will see darkness.
They will see gloom.
They will see anguish.
They will be driven away.
They will enter utter darkness.
passages.original: וְאֶל־ אֶ֖רֶץ יַבִּ֑יט וְהִנֵּ֨ה צָרָ֤ה וַחֲשֵׁכָה֙ מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה וַאֲפֵלָ֖ה מְנֻדָּֽח׃
